france24fr.description: Il y a 90 ans, la guerre d'Espagne (1/4). À l'été 1936, le coup d'État lancé par Francisco Franco plonge l'Espagne dans une guerre qui dépasse rapidement ses frontières. Les militaires insurgés, soutenus par Hitler et Mussolini, et les républicains, abandonnés par les démocraties occidentales, s'opposent dans un conflit qui pour certains apparaît comme annonciateur de la Seconde Guerre mondiale.

france24fr.title: Russie : le géant de l'e-commerce Wildberries visé par une nouvelle attaque ukrainienne
france24fr.description: Un site logistique de la plateforme de commerce en ligne Wildberries a été touché dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi par une frappe ukrainienne, à environ 180 km à l'est de Moscou. Depuis mi-juillet, l'Ukraine a frappé une vingtaine de sites appartenant à l'"Amazon russe" dans presque toute la Russie et en Crimée annexée.

france24fr.title: Le jour où Yves Saint Laurent a choqué le monde de la haute couture
france24fr.description: Saviez-vous qu'Yves Saint Laurent a popularisé la mode rétro ? Au prix d'une très grande polémique… Retour sur « la collection du scandale » de 1971, à l'occasion des 90 ans de la naissance du couturier français.

france24fr.title: Cuba : sixième panne d'électricité nationale depuis le début de l'année
france24fr.description: Une nouvelle panne d'électricité est en cours à Cuba, survenue dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi, quelques heures après le rétablissement du courant à la suite d'un précédent black-out, ont fait savoir les autorités. Les coupures de courant se sont aggravées dans l'île depuis janvier, lorsque Washington a imposé un blocus pétrolier à l'île.

france24fr.title: Incendies en Grèce : situation "extrêmement difficile", plus de 12 000 hectares ravagés
france24fr.description: La Grèce, confrontée à plusieurs violents incendies, fait face à une situation "extrêmement difficile", a prévenu dimanche le Premier ministre Kyriakos Mitsotakis. En une semaine, plus de 12 000 hectares de forêts et de terres agricoles ont brûlé dans ce pays touché de plein fouet par la crise climatique, comme l'ensemble du pourtour méditerranéen. Les précisions d'Alexia Kefalas, correspondante de France 24 à Athènes.

france24fr.title: Fifa : Gianni Infantino sous pression après l'échec de son nouveau projet
france24fr.description: Gianni Infantino, le président de la fédération internationale de football, est sous pression après l’abandon du projet Fifa Forward Entreprise. Il pourrait perdre son poste avant mars 2027, date de la prochaine élection de la fédération.

france24fr.title: Drame de Ceuta: "Les projectiles humains de Mohammed VI"
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce lundi 3 août, les réactions aux derniers bilans officiels des migrants morts en tentant de rejoindre l’enclave espagnole de Ceuta depuis le Maroc: 11 morts selon les autorités marocaines, au moins 72 selon les autorités espagnoles. Un drame qui fracture l’UE. La fronde de l’UEFA contre le patron de la Fifa, Gianni Infantino, malgré l’abandon de son projet d’ouvrir une partie de ses activités commerciales aux investisseurs privés. Et des surfeurs qui ont du chien.

france24fr.title: Un week-end marqué par les frappes israéliennes sur Gaza
france24fr.description: Il ne reste plus qu'un tas de ferraille d'une voiture de le centre de Gaza, visée par une attaque dimanche. De nouvelles frappes israéliennes à travers la bande de Gaza ont fait une dizaine de morts selon la Défense civile dimanche, quelques jours après l'annonce d'un accord sur le désarmement du mouvement islamiste Hamas et le retrait israélien du territoire palestinien. Depuis samedi, l'enclave connaît une recrudescence des attaques.

france24fr.title: Brésil : Lula lance sa dernière campagne présidentielle
france24fr.description: Panama sur la tête, Lula s'affiche fidèle à lui-même. Ce routier de la politique a lancé sa dernière campagne, dimanche, lors d'une convention de son parti, le PT, à Sao Paulo. Devant ses partisans, il a défendu sa bonne santé, et vanté sa bonne forme physique due au sport. Il s'est aussi montré combattif sur des sujets polémiques, comme les terres rares. Une campagne axée sur la souveraineté du Brésil, un thème qui plaît à ses partisans.

france24fr.title: Polémique autour du bilan des migrants décédés à Ceuta
france24fr.description: De nombreuses familles cherchent leurs proches après la traversée dramatique et meurtrière à Ceuta. Selon l'Espagne, 72 migrants ont perdu la vie. Mais, au Maroc, d'autres bilans sont médiatisés - notamment par l'ONDH. Les autorités marocaines ont alors décidé, dimanche soir, de s'exprimer, faisant état de 11 morts et déplorant une désinformation autour de cette crise.

france24fr.title: Trois feux de forêt dévastateurs ravagent Spokane, dans le nord-ouest américain
france24fr.description: Les flammes de trois incendies, toujours actifs, ont parcouru Spokane et ses environs, dans l'État américain de Washington, dimanche. Ils ont détruit plusieurs centaines de bâtiments et entraîné des évacuations massives, sans faire de victime.

france24fr.title: Une frappe de drone fait au moins 35 morts dans le Darfour au Soudan, selon Emergency Lawyers
france24fr.description: Selon l'ONG Emergency Lawyers, une frappe a visé le tribunal du village de Garra al-Zawaya, dans l'État du Darfour du Nord, au Soudan, dimanche, où des civils "étaient réunis". Elle fait état d'au moins 35 personnes tuées. Le gouvernement autoproclamé des Forces de soutien rapide a condamné cette attaque, la qualifiant de "crime horrible".

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis sont intervenus pour soutenir le yen, Donald Trump évoque un "geste d'amitié"
france24fr.description: Le Financial Times a affirmé dimanche que "la Réserve fédérale de New York a(vait) pris la décision inhabituelle de procéder à une vente d'euros pour acheter des yens pour le compte du Trésor" vendredi, en coordination avec le Japon. Une intervention confirmée par le président américain, qui évoque un "geste d'amitié" et un "avantage financier".

france24fr.title: En direct : Israël transmet aux États-Unis ses "inquiétudes" sur le plan pour Gaza
france24fr.description: Israël a fait part aux Américains de ses "inquiétudes" concernant le plan sur le désarmement du Hamas pour mettre fin à la guerre à Gaza, annoncé par Donald Trump. En Iran, la diplomatie a démenti toute négociation en cours avec Washington, au lendemain des déclarations du président américain affirmant qu'elles devaient reprendre cet après-midi. Suivez la situation en direct.

france24fr.title: Pourquoi certains États veulent quitter la Cour Pénale internationale
france24fr.description: Après le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger, le Tchad a annoncé le 27 juillet son retrait de la Cour pénale internationale. C’est une nouvelle étape dans la stratégie diplomatique de ces États du Sahel. Après leur départ de la CEDEAO et de l'OIF, les Etats de l’AES dénoncent désormais une institution qu'elles jugent instrumentalisée par les puissances occidentales.

france24fr.title: Pourquoi le Mali, le Burkina Faso, le Niger et le Tchad quittent-ils la Cour pénale internationale ?
france24fr.description: Le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger ont annoncé leur retrait de la Cour pénale internationale. Les trois pays de l'Alliance des États du Sahel dénoncent une justice internationale qu'ils jugent partiale et instrumentalisée. Cette décision soulève des questions majeures : quelles conséquences pour les enquêtes en cours ? Quel impact pour les victimes des conflits au Sahel ? france24fr.title: Présidentielle au Brésil : Lula candidat pour un quatrième et dernier mandat à la tête du pays
france24fr.description: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva s'est porté candidat, dimanche, à un quatrième et dernier mandat à la tête du Brésil lors d'une convention de son Parti des travailleurs à Sao Paulo. À 80 ans, le président brésilien s'est dit "en pleine forme".

france24fr.title: Tour de France Femmes, étape 2 : Wiebes récidive au sprint et conforte son maillot jaune
france24fr.description: Déjà victorieuse la veille à Lausanne, Lorena Wiebes a récidivé dimanche en remportant la deuxième étape du Tour de France Femmes à Genève. La cycliste néerlandaise de la formation SDS Worx a devancé au sprint l'Italienne Elisa Balsamo et la Néerlandaise Marianne Vos, confortant son maillot jaune.

nzz.description: Laut amtlichen Daten sind Spitzensaläre und Verwaltungskosten bei den Versicherern leicht gesunken. Das Hauptproblem bleiben jedoch die Gesundheitskosten.

letemps.title: Canadair, une histoire faite de nombreuses et parfois violentes turbulences
letemps.description:
Le célèbre bombardier d’eau, devenu un outil essentiel de la lutte contre les incendies, est issu d’une histoire industrielle mouvementée. De son invention au Canada à l’arrêt de sa production, puis à sa relance sous un nouveau nom, retour sur les tribulations d’un avion aujourd’hui très convoité

Les étés européens sont désormais familiers de la silhouette des canadairs. Lorsqu’un incend

spiegel.title: Heizungsgesetz: Warum neue Gasheizungen zur Kostenfalle werden könnten
spiegel.description: Das neue Heizungsgesetz ermöglicht wieder den Einbau von Öl- und Gasheizungen. Doch die könnten zur Kostenfalle werden. Hier können Mieter, Vermieter und Eigentümer schauen, was auf sie zukommt.

spiegel.title: Iran: Zwei Männer wegen angeblicher Spionage für Israel hingerichtet
spiegel.description: Seit Kriegsbeginn häufen sich in Iran die Hinrichtungen wegen mutmaßlicher Spionage. Nun wurden zwei weitere Männer gehängt, denen die Justiz Zusammenarbeit mit dem Mossad vorwirft.

spiegel.title: Künstliche Intelligenz: Kriminelle nutzen zunehmend KI für Hacker-Angriffe
spiegel.description: Ein neuer Bericht legt nahe, dass mehr KI-Bots als Menschen hinter Hackingattacken stecken. IT-Experten warnen besonders vor einer neuen Masche – gegen die sich aufmerksame Onlinenutzer aber schützen können.

spiegel.title: Dax steigt auf Rekordhoch
spiegel.description: Gefallene Ölpreise haben dem deutschen Aktienmarkt einen starken Monatsstart beschert. Der Dax stieg zum Handelsauftakt auf 25.912,59 Punkte.

spiegel.title: Klimaschutz in Städten und Kommunen: Das Ende der Klima-Euphorie
spiegel.description: Schwerin, Bottrop, Jena und viele andere Städte kassieren ihre ehrgeizigen CO₂-Einsparziele. War der »Klimanotstand« nur Gerede?

spiegel.title: Hitze und extreme Temperaturen: Jochen Flasbarth fordert Hitzeaktionsplan für 2027
spiegel.description: Süddeutschland steht eine weitere Hitzewoche bevor. Für den kommenden Sommer will der SPD-Politiker Jochen Flasbarth Deutschland besser gegen Extremtemperaturen wappnen.

spiegel.title: WTA-Turnier in Memphis: 16 Jahre alte Kristina Ljutowa gewinnt bei Debüt
spiegel.description: Erstes Turnier, erster Titel: Kristina Ljutowa gelingt ein Traumstart in die Profikarriere, jünger war bei einem Erfolg zuletzt Coco Gauff 2019. In der Weltrangliste klettert die junge Russin um mehr als 100 Plätze.

spiegel.title: Athen: Frauenleiche in Koffer gefunden - Tatverdächtiger in Haft
spiegel.description: Nach dem Fund einer Frauenleiche in Athen hat die Polizei einen Tatverdächtigen ermittelt. Der Mann soll die 38-jährige Schottin getötet, in einem Koffer verstaut und dann Geld von ihren Konten abgehoben haben.

spiegel.title: Elektro-Mobilität: Hersteller gewähren weniger Rabatte auf E-Autos
spiegel.description: Die Nachfrage nach Elektroautos wächst. So gut, dass Kaufanreize offenbar überflüssig werden. Die Hersteller jedenfalls knausern zunehmend mit Rabatten.

spiegel.title: Tonda Eckert: Trainer des FC Southampton spricht nach Spionage-Skandal über Morddrohungen
spiegel.description: Der FC Southampton wurde aus den Aufstiegs-Playoffs zur Premier League ausgeschlossen, weil Trainer Tonda Eckert gegnerische Clubs ausspähen ließ. Nun hat sich der Deutsche zu den Auswirkungen geäußert.

spiegel.title: Bio-Lebensmittel: Nachfrage wächst trotz hoher Preise im zweiten Quartal
spiegel.description: Die Inflation zwingt Verbraucher zur sorgfältigen Planung ihrer Ausgaben. Trotzdem kaufen sie zunehmend Biolebensmittel. Das hat auch mit den großen Anbietern zu tun.

spiegel.title: Friedrich II. machte Preußen zur Großmacht: Welche Opfer seine Soldaten dafür bringen mussten
spiegel.description: Hohenzollernkönig Friedrich II. machte aus dem kargen Preußen im 18. Jahrhundert eine Großmacht und wurde zum Helden. Lange wurde übersehen, welche Opfer seine Soldaten dafür auf dem Schlachtfeld bringen mussten.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Der Iran-Krieg erreicht die USA - Cyberattacken gegen Wasserversorgung
spiegel.description: Wassersysteme in mehreren US-Bundesstaaten sind Ziel eines Hackerangriffs geworden. Ermittler haben Iran im Verdacht. Der Präsident verdrängt die Vorfälle, so gut er kann, doch der Krieg holt ihn ein.

spiegel.title: News: Ceuta, Rentenreform, Steffen Bilger, CDU-Aufregung um Dieter Hallervorden
spiegel.description: Die Kurzzeit-Migrationskrise in Ceuta hat ein europäisches Nachspiel. Die Rentenreform der Koalition beginnt zu wackeln. Und der neue Verkehrsminister Steffen Bilger legt los. Das ist die Lage am Montagmorgen.

spiegel.title: David Safier: Nach Angela Merkel jetzt Armin Laschet – warum lieben die Deutschen alberne Politikerkrimis?
Gehaltsverhandlungen: Wie Sie trotz Sparzwang mehr Geld herausholen
spiegel.description: Konjunktur am Boden, Gelder eingefroren, KI im Nacken: Über das Gehalt zu sprechen, fühlt sich schwierig an. Doch wer schweigt, verliert. Zwei Experten erklären, wie die Gehaltsverhandlung aktuell gelingen kann.

spiegel.title: Karriere-Netzwerke: Zugang zum verdeckten Arbeitsmarkt ohne peinliche Selbstinszenierung
spiegel.description: Ein gutes Netzwerk ist oft der einzige Zugang zum verdeckten Arbeitsmarkt. Dabei ist »Vitamin B« keine Frage von Glück oder Herkunft: Beziehungspflege ist lernbar.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump bestätigt: USA helfen Japan bei schwächelndem Yen
spiegel.description: Der Yen war zuletzt stark unter Druck geraten. Um die Währung zu stützen, haben Tokio und Washington gemeinsam am Devisenmarkt interveniert – erstmals seit Jahrzehnten. US-Präsident Trump spricht von einem »Zeichen der Freundschaft«.

observador.title: 9h. Irão diz não estar a negociar com EUA
observador.description: O ministro iraniano dos Negócios Estrangeiros avisa que acordo com Omã não é suficiente para reabrir o estreito. Ainda, Espanha aponta responsabilidades a Marrocos na entrada de migrantes em Ceuta.

observador.title: Geografia, cerveja e as audições fantasma da nossa política
observador.description: Ceuta em Lisboa, "finos" comunistas e o Chega a fugir da audição. Pelo meio, no Avante, a salada russa gera uma crise ideológica sobre o feijão frade.

observador.title: As histórias dos doentes contadas pelos próprios
observador.description: Na quarta temporada da secção Mental trazemos uma novidade especial: as histórias dos doentes, contadas na primeira pessoa.

observador.title: Nova rede de transportes em Trás-os-Montes arranca hoje
observador.description: Autarca destaca "investimento muito grande" em serviço público de transporte. Gratuito até setembro, representa investimento de 5 milhões de euros, suportado por municípios. Exigem justiça ao Governo.

observador.title: A invasão de Ceuta é um aviso e um alerta para toda a Europa
observador.description: A vaga humana que submergiu Ceuta não criou só um desafio para Espanha, obriga a Europa a discutir a garantia das fronteiras externas e a coerência das políticas internas de acolhimento de imigrantes.

observador.title: Ministro da Educação ouvido no Parlamento sobre exames
observador.description: Fernando Alexandre marca presença em reunião extraordinária da Comissão Permanente para discutir “a situação dos exames nacionais", às 15h.

observador.title: Farpas no Dragão e Vini já está em modo Mourinho
observador.description: As picardias entre FC Porto e Benfica continuam, o US Open choca com bilhetes exorbitantes e Vozinha vive 40 dias de viragem total.

observador.title: Kennedy e Giulia Be: O casório que vai parar o Rio
observador.description: Connor Kennedy e Giulia Be levam o clã todo para o Rio com um casamento em que até Lula e Trump são convidados. E ainda, o escândalo do restaurante que maltratava pessoas.

observador.title: 8h. Ceuta. Serviços de informação espanhóis acusam Marrocos
observador.description: O primeiro relatório do governo espanhol sobre a crise de Ceuta diz que Marrocos facilitou entrada de imigrantes. Ainda, ministro da Educação é hoje chamado ao Parlamento sobre exames nacionais.

observador.title: Crise migratória em Ceuta e o plano pessoal de Infantino
observador.description: Ceuta viu entrar milhares de migrantes de um dia para o outro, alimentados por mensagens nas redes sociais de que a fronteira estava aberta. Este é um dos temas do dia.

observador.title: Trump anuncia novas negociações com o Irão
observador.description: No sábado, na rede social Truth, Trump revelou que os aliados dos Estados Unidos no Médio Oriente chegaram a um entendimento sobre os termos de um acordo para pôr fim à guerra com o Irão.

observador.title: Sudão. Ataque de drone mata 35 pessoas
observador.description: Além das mortes, ataque também danificou o edifício do tribunal, uma instituição tradicional utilizada para resolver disputas locais e tribais, indicou o Emergency Lawyers, um grupo independente.

observador.title: Lula da Silva é o único trunfo da esquerda no Brasil?
observador.description: Sem alternativas capazes de rivalizar com o carisma de Lula no Brasil, a esquerda aposta no "cromo repetido". Já do outro lado do Atlântico, a Europa racha ao meio com o caos migratório.

observador.title: "Ucrânia não tem, neste momento, como se defender"
observador.description: Francisco Pereira Coutinho avisa que falta de mísseis Patriot é um problema gravíssimo. O especialista em direito internacional afirma que as ameaças de Trump ao Irão são cíclicas.

observador.title: “Fui aprender a ser artista (para depois desaprender!)”
observador.description: A nova exposição de Manuela Pimentel na Underdogs traz cartazes velhos que resgata da rua e faz arte nobre do que é pobre, faz belo o que é feio, e convida-nos a desacelerar e a contemplar as cidades.

observador.title: Mulher de Jair Bolsonaro candidata ao Senado brasileiro
observador.description: Ex-primeira-dama brasileira não compareceu ao lançamento da candidatura, devido a problemas de saúde. Michelle Bolsonaro é considerada uma figura-chave para atrair o eleitorado feminino.

observador.title: Superniño. Delcy Rodríguez apela à poupança de água e luz
observador.description: Delcy Rodríguez disse ter pedido "planos específicos" para enfrentar o aumento das temperaturas devido ao fenómeno "Superniño". Apelou ainda aos venezuelanos para pouparem energia elétrica e água.

observador.title: Vozinha "muito feliz" por assinar pelo Colo-Colo, do Chile
observador.description: Guarda-redes dos "Tubarões Azuis" chegou a Santiago do Chile, recebido por adeptos do clube. Teve dois atrasos consecutivos na chegada ao país. Deverá assinar por seis meses, podendo renovar até 2027.

elpais.title: Juan Jesús Vivas, presidente de Ceuta: “Marruecos ha demostrado que no es fiable, hay que exigirle respeto”
elpais.description: El dirigente confía en la fortaleza de pertenecer a Europa y se mantiene inflexible en la defensa de los musulmanes y en el reparto legal de menores en la Península

elpais.title: Última hora de la entrada de inmigrantes a Ceuta, en directo | Albares carga contra la “internacional reaccionaria” y considera la desinformación el elemento clave de la crisis en Ceuta
elpais.description: El Gobierno asegura que “exigirá solidaridad” de los Estados de la UE y reitera que Marruecos colaboró “desde el primer momento”

elpais.title: Vallas de obra para cerrar las calles y batidas para ahuyentar a los migrantes que se resisten a dejar Ceuta: “Todavía quedan”
elpais.description: Muchos jóvenes migrantes son expulsados de los barrios por vecinos y militares y optan por esconderse en una zona de embalses y bosque

elpais.title: Los servicios de inteligencia concluyen que Rabat permitió y utilizó la oleada humana sobre Ceuta, pero no la planeó
elpais.description: La Moncloa no ha reunido el gabinete de crisis, pese a calificar lo sucedido de “violación de la integridad territorial”

elpais.title: Así amanece Ceuta cuatro días después de la crisis migratoria
elpais.description: Las imágenes muestran a migrantes descansando en la orilla de la playa, cerca de los cordones policiales, mientras que las fuerzas de seguridad mantienen una presencia visible

elpais.title: Marruecos admite 11 muertos en su territorio tras la avalancha en Ceuta y se presenta como un socio “fiable y responsable”
elpais.description: El Ejecutivo marroquí achaca la tragedia en la ciudad autónoma a las “malas interpretaciones” de la sentencia del Supremo

elpais.title: Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo: “Todavía no he entendido lo de Ayuso y el ático”
elpais.description: La diputada del PP confiesa que no lee mucho los argumentarios del partido y que le gustaría ser ministra: “Estoy aquí para hacer gran política, no para ser una espectadora”

elpais.title: La desconocida vida de los trabajadores que habitaban el Palacio Real: “Suplico se me conceda el cuarto que ha dejado la doncella Antonia”
elpais.description: EL PAÍS accede a la documentación, planos y cartas que detallan el día a día de los empleados palaciegos, desde que se levantó el edificio a mediados del siglo XVIII hasta el final del franquismo

elpais.title: ‘Anfetas’ para trabajar, saludos nazis y un compañero muerto: así fue el “Erasmus” de los Beatles en Hamburgo
elpais.description: Un libro y un nuevo documental exploran los turbulentos años que la banda de Liverpool pasó ganándose la vida en Alemania antes de alcanzar la  fama, donde conformaron su imagen y estilo

elpais.title: Por qué Jon Bernthal es el perfecto tipo duro de Hollywood: una formación rusa, dos hermanos demasiado modélicos y 15 roturas de nariz
elpais.description: El ganador del Emmy acaba de demostrar su vena guerrera en ‘La Odisea’ y lo nuevo de ‘Spider-Man’. Su convincente aura de malote está forjada en mil batallas dentro y fuera del set, hasta casi acabar en la cárcel. Una profesora, su familia y cursos de control de la ira le ayudaron a escoger un camino menos problemático

elpais.title: ¿Por qué somos (casi todos) diestros? Dos millones de años de misterio evolutivo
elpais.description: No hay una sola causa, sino varias de ellas, entrelazadas. La hipótesis con más fuerza apunta al desarrollo de nuestro cerebro y al origen del lenguaje: los gestos

elpais.title: Las pastillas han conseguido que te salgan bien los análisis, pero ¿estás sano de verdad?
elpais.description: Un estudio muestra que los medicamentos han logrado que las personas con obesidad tengan el colesterol y la tensión en niveles saludables

elpais.title: Los estadounidenses tienen menos de cien días para salvar su democracia
elpais.description: Una avalancha al estilo húngaro es lo único que podrá desbaratar los intentos de Donald Trump de amañar las elecciones de mitad de mandato

elpais.title: Lo de la IA fugada
elpais.description: Es mejor no repetir el relato de Sam Altman sobre el incidente con la inteligencia artificial y tratar de separar el mito de los hechos

elpais.title: El jefe de la UME: “A los grandes incendios forestales no se les puede atacar, solo nos podemos defender”
elpais.description: “Un fuego que avanza a 15 metros por minuto está fuera de control. El de Ávila y Madrid corría a 60”, explica el teniente general Francisco Javier Marcos

elpais.title: El PP entierra el pacto de Estado pese a que su plan antiincendios coincide en buena parte con el del Gobierno
elpais.description: Expertos consultados por EL PAÍS señalan las medidas imprescindibles. El secretario de Estado de Medio Ambiente ve “un amplio espacio para el acuerdo”

elpais.title: Dentro del corazón quemado del parque natural de la Sierra de Espadán
elpais.description: El incendio de la Vall d’Uixó ha dejado 3.750 hectáreas convertidas en un paisaje de ceniza, árboles carbonizados y humo que aún emerge del suelo una semana después

elpais.title: Gironda, el incendio que desbordó a Francia: “Sin la solidaridad internacional, habría sido dramático”
elpais.description: El fuego desatado hace 10 días en el suroeste de Francia, el mayor desde la II Guerra Mundial, ha obligado a evacuar a 220.000 personas y ha abierto el debate sobre la falta de adaptación al cambio climático

republika.title: Alcaraz, allenamento con il cono sull’occhio e ritorno a Cincinnati. Intanto è di nuovo numero 2
republika.description: Lo spagnolo scavalca Zverev alla vigilia del Masters nell’Ohio che segnerà il ritorno in campo dopo quattro mesi. Sedute particolari per tornare subito al top

republika.title: Italia nella morsa del caldo, oggi 25 le città in rosso. Allerta gialla per il maltempo al Sud
republika.description: Abruzzo, Sicilia e Umbria a rischio temporali. Punte di 40 gradi almeno per un’altra settimana

republika.title: Quei sorvoli in quota inseguendo il mistero delle linee di Nazca
republika.description: I loro significato è oggetto di dibattito. Molti sostengono che fossero sentieri da usare durante le cerimonie religiose o per riti propiziatori legati ai raccolti. Per altri hanno un significato astronomico

republika.title: Anche se sei Rooney devi metterti a studiare
republika.description: Lo hanno sepolto di aggettivi per le guance rosse, i chili di troppo e i vestiti tagliati male. Ha cambiato stile, si è rimesso in forma e si è informato anche sui dettagli della regia, diventando la vera rivelazione dei palinsesti grazie a un linguaggio diretto e privo di filtri

republika.title: L’esperto: “Rabat ha organizzato tutto è un avvertimento a Madrid”
republika.description: Pierr Vermeren: “Quei giovani disperati non hanno potuto arrivare lì da soli: per la monarchia, le due exclave sono solo il frutto del colonialismo”

republika.title: Migranti, pressing dell’Italia per aprire hub extra-Ue nel 2027
republika.description: Oggi a Bruxelles, al vertice degli ambasciatori, Roma cerca sponde per accelerare su centri europei operativi prima delle elezioni. L’asse con Merz e la socialista danese Frederiksen

republika.title: Centri rimpatri all’estero costosi fallimenti in serie dal Ruanda all’Albania
republika.description: La Gran Bretagna per prima ha tentato di esternalizzare in Africa le strutture. La Danimarca ci prova in Kosovo. Finora non ha funzionato

republika.title: Ceuta, allarme bambini: sono migliaia i minori arrivati dal Marocco
republika.description: Mille e cinquecento nei centri di accoglienza, altrettanti fuori tra i corpi che il mare restituisce anche quelli di piccoli schiacciati

republika.title: Cresce la paura dello straniero cavalcata dagli slogan della Lega
republika.description:
Per otto elettori su dieci del Carroccio gli immigrati
sono un pericolo. Chi vota per i partiti di centrosinistra chiede un Paese più aperto

republika.title: Bin Salman ferma i raid Usa. Trump: “Oggi nuovi colloqui”
republika.description: Telefonata del principe saudita alla Casa Bianca: “Compiere ogni sforzo per la tregua”. Voci di un attacco preventivo dei pasdaran

republika.title: Stati Uniti, scontro tra le anime Dem così i progressisti rischiano di dividere i propri elettori
republika.description: Domani primarie decisive in Michigan: un medico socialista di origini egiziane sfida la figlia del Midwest bianco e moderato. Un duello senza esclusione di colpi da cui dipendono le speranze dell’Asinello di riconquistare il Senato e mettere un freno a Trump alle midterm

republika.title: Ignatieff: “La società civile impedirà i brogli elettorali, le istituzioni sono solide”
republika.description: Lo storico statunitense: “Il rischio di manipolazioni c’è sempre, ma c’è un sistema a difesa della democrazia: dai volontari, agli scrutatori agli avvocati”

republika.title: Le radici della destra e la fatica a digerire le verità processuali
republika.description: Le ripetute negazioni dei dirigenti FdI, dalla pista palestinese alla difesa dei condannati

republika.title: Strage stazione di Bologna, Meloni omette e La Russa non si rassegna alla matrice neofascista
republika.description: Il messaggio di Mattarella: “Libertà, giustizia, democrazia. I valori che la strategia neofascista voleva distruggere”

republika.title: Il giudice: “Le sentenze hanno provato il filo nero tra i condannati e la strategia della tensione”
republika.description: Raffaello Magi, relatore della sentenza definitiva che ha confermato l’ergastolo a Cavallini: “I depistaggi furono evidenti”

republika.title: Strage di Bologna, l’ultimo appiglio di Cavallini è nel Dna riesumato da una vittima
republika.description: L’ex Nar sostiene la presenza di un’altra persona. I legali dei familiari : “Ipotesi priva di fondamento”. Il 15 ottobre l’udienza

republika.title: L’Odissea dell’ex Ilva: ormai nessuno è più dispostoa comprare e investire
republika.description: Il polo di Taranto è un paradigma delle incapacità del Paese: fallimento industriale e accanimento giudiziario. Colpa della latitanza della politica

republika.title: La Brianza sotto shock per la tragedia in Perù: “Due famiglie distrutte”
republika.description: La coppia di manager, l’imprenditore e la moglie, i tre figli. Erano partiti insieme: “Quel viaggio era stato il loro unico lusso”

nyt.title: Blanche Gives G.O.P. Senators Written Assurances on Trump’s I.R.S. Deal
nyt.description: Todd Blanche’s confirmation as attorney general has been held up over concerns about a planned $1.8 billion fund for Trump allies and the president’s immunity from tax scrutiny.

nyt.title: New Round of Trump Threats and Pullbacks Raises Uncertainty in Mideast
nyt.description: Analysts and lawmakers are trying to divine whether Mr. Trump’s latest announcement means negotiations with Iran will truly get underway Monday or if the president is just working through unappealing options.

nyt.title: Fact-Checking Trump’s Claims About the Effect of the Iran War on Oil Prices, Munitions and More
nyt.description: The president misleadingly blamed the Biden administration’s weapons transfers to Ukraine for current concerns over munitions stockpiles, among other claims about the Iran war.

nyt.title: Ceuta Migration Crisis Exposes Despair Among Morocco’s Young People
nyt.description: Moroccan migrants described their despair at their economic future, explaining what propelled them across the border with Spain.

nyt.title: How China Keeps Tabs on Foreigners
nyt.description: An unsecured police dashboard was a rare window into how the authorities track foreigners by collecting and aggregating vast amounts of private data.

nyt.title: As France’s Elders Swelter in the Heat, Postal Workers Come to the Rescue
nyt.description: To help prevent heat-related deaths, the French government has asked postal workers to check in on older people.

nyt.title: U.S. and Japan Coordinated to Help Stabilize the Yen
nyt.description: U.S. and Japanese officials confirmed that the Treasury Department had moved last week to prop up the currency, which had been trading near four-decade lows.

nyt.title: How a Top Law Firm Went From Standing Up to Trump to Bending the Knee
nyt.description: Paul Weiss was a progressive stalwart for decades and led the legal resistance against President Trump in his first term. Then it surrendered without a fight. This is the inside story of its transformation.

nyt.title: Trump, Paul Weiss and the Capitulation of Big Law: 5 Takeaways
nyt.description: The law firm Paul Weiss led the legal resistance against President Trump. Then it led a sudden retreat across the legal industry. A Times investigation examined how it caved to White House pressure.

nyt.title: Ohio Senator Calls Former Son-in-Law Accused of Abuse Unfit for Office
nyt.description: Senator Bernie Moreno, Republican of Ohio, broke his silence about allegations of domestic abuse his daughter has made against Representative Max Miller.

nyt.title: ‘Comradely’ Talks and a ‘Deer Leader’ Mascot: Scenes From the D.S.A. Summit
nyt.description: At a national meeting of the Democratic Socialists of America, nervous energy and a sprawling tableau of sometimes-competing interests were on display.

nyt.title: Spokane Wildfires Destroy Hundreds of Buildings as Thousands Evacuate
nyt.description: Firefighters were hopeful that improving weather conditions in Washington state could help efforts to contain the blaze, which officials described as the largest natural disaster in the history of Spokane.

nyt.title: Gunman Acted Alone in Idaho In-N-Out Attack, Authorities Say
nyt.description: An off-duty state trooper and private citizen returned fire and are credited with slowing the 24-year-old shooter.

nyt.title: What We Know About the Shooting at an In-N-Out Burger in Idaho
nyt.description: Gunfire brought panic to a shopping center in Twin Falls in what the authorities described as a chaotic scene. At least three people were killed.

nyt.title: Plug-In Solar Panels Are Starting to Sprout in U.S. Backyards
nyt.description: Ten U.S. states have legalized systems that can be plugged into standard wall outlets. The technology typically does not require permits or electricians.

nyt.title: What You Need to Know About Installing Plug-In Solar Panels
nyt.description: You can now buy panels that plug into electrical outlets, but there are some important safety issues to consider when picking and installing a system.

nyt.title: Cowboys Fringants Bassist Is Named Quebec’s Chief Scientist
nyt.description: Jérôme Dupras is a member of one of Quebec’s most popular folk rock bands. Now, as the province’s chief scientist, he will help shape its environmental destiny.

nyt.title: The War That Could Swallow the World
nyt.description: Whatever is happening in Iran, it isn’t working.

npr.title: Israel says it has serious concerns with Hamas disarmament deal

phys-org.title: South Korea records its highest-ever temperature of 42.5 C
phys-org.description: South Korea registered its highest temperature since records began more than a century ago on Sunday, as authorities warned people to "immediately" stop all outdoor activities in affected areas.

phys-org.title: August's total solar eclipse will sweep over Spain, Iceland and Greenland
phys-org.description: For the first time in more than a century, a total solar eclipse is coming to mainland Spain with an even longer encore next summer.

phys-org.title: How fitness, speed and position shape competition in expanding populations
phys-org.description: A study published in the Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment (JSTAT), inspired by the behavior of bacterial colonies observed in previous experiments, uses mathematical models to describe the expansion of competing populations. The aim is to understand which factors determine the success of one population over another.

phys-org.title: Rideshare launches boost regional GDP and flexible jobs, study finds
phys-org.description: Ride-hailing has become a routine part of urban life in the United States, but its broader economic impacts have been difficult to measure. As Uber and Lyft expanded across hundreds of cities over the past decade, they promised more flexible work for drivers and convenience for passengers. Questions remained, however, about how these promises translated into measurable changes in local economies.

phys-org.title: Mom or not, caring for babies changes the brain
phys-org.description: Freeman Hrabowski Scholar Bianca Jones Marlin studies how caregiving takes shape in the brain and how some biological adaptations are passed to the next generation.

phys-org.title: A cooperative approach to reproductive success
phys-org.description: Fertilization is often imagined as a frantic race, with millions of sperm competing for a single prize. But new research by a team of evolutionary biologists from Syracuse University, the University of Siena in Italy and the University of Szeged in Hungary reveals a more surprising reality, where success can depend less on competition and more on cooperation.

phys-org.title: Newly unearthed mechanism that helps plants 'feel full' could help crops use fertilizer more efficiently
phys-org.description: New York University researchers have pinpointed the molecular players responsible for plants "feeling full" once they've taken up enough nitrogen—a finding that could help scientists develop plants that absorb more nitrogen from the soil and allow farmers to reduce environmentally and economically costly fertilizer applications.

phys-org.title: How simple amber lights could make nights safer for insects
phys-org.description: Approximately 40% of insect species worldwide are thought to be in decline and under threat of extinction. Among the key causes are habitat loss, pollution and climate change. Another threat is artificial light from sources like streetlights and security lamps. In new research published in the journal Biological Conservation, scientists say a simple change in artificial lighting could help reduce this particular threat.

phys-org.title: Climate change could dramatically reduce water flowing from the West's headwaters
phys-org.description: The small mountain streams that feed many of the West's rivers may face a much drier future. A new study led by NAU researchers found that groundwater-fed streamflow, known as base flow, has been steadily declining across headwater watersheds in the western United States since 1950 and could decrease by 45% to 65% by the end of this century if current climate trends continue.

phys-org.title: New microscopy method achieves angstrom-scale localization precision with one laser
phys-org.description: Researchers in the lab of Sam Peng, the Pfizer Inc.–Gerald Laubach Career Development Assistant Professor of Chemistry at MIT and a core institute member of the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard, have developed a super-resolution imaging technology. It allows scientists to visualize molecular structures with angstrom-level localization precision—three orders of magnitude beyond the nanometer-scale limits of standard fluorescent dyes—while simplifying the imaging process.

phys-org.title: Antibiotic resistance is spreading through South Africa's water systems. This study explains how
phys-org.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is defined as the ability of disease-causing microorganisms to withstand treatments like antibiotics.

phys-org.title: Webb reveals warped structure in nearby TW Hydrae's protoplanetary disk
phys-org.description: Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers obtained high-contrast coronagraphic images of the protoplanetary disk around the young, nearby star TW Hydrae. Results of the observational campaign, published July 27 on the preprint server arXiv, shed more light on the nature of this disk.

phys-org.title: Supergene solves evolutionary puzzle of mirror-image flowers
phys-org.description: The left-right asymmetry of South African butterfly lilies (genus Wachendorfia) has been regarded as a classic evolutionary puzzle for more than a century. Due to the mirror-image arrangement of the floral parts, the plants achieve efficient cross-pollination. The molecular basis of this arrangement has now been uncovered by an international team led by the University of Potsdam.

phys-org.title: Why some nitrogen-processing enzymes are more efficient than others
phys-org.description: Nitrogen gas is abundant in Earth's atmosphere, but most living organisms can't readily use it. Only a subset of microbes with enzymes known as nitrogenases can break nitrogen gas apart and convert it into ammonia.

phys-org.title: Laid to rest with care: Ancient infants, perhaps twins, found in 1,200-year-old latrine
phys-org.description: More than 1,000 years ago, two babies were tucked away in an abandoned Roman toilet channel. Yet, despite what the location suggests, they were cherished, not discarded.

phys-org.title: AI use mirrors student schedules in study of 77,000 online learners
phys-org.description: How do students actually use AI learning assistants? A new research paper by IU International University of Applied Sciences provides the first robust answers to this question. For the study "Using AI-based Learning Assistants in Higher Education: A Large-Scale Descriptive Analysis," the research team led by Prof. Dr.-Ing. Kristina Schaaff, Dr. Valerie Hekkel and Quintus Stierstorfer analyzed anonymized usage data from approximately 77,000 IU online students who were using the Learning Companion

phys-org.title: Forever chemicals and pesticides under Trump: what to know
phys-org.description: Since returning to power, President Donald Trump's administration has approved five pesticides considered by many to be PFAS "forever chemicals," a class of toxic substances facing bans and increasing restrictions around the world.

phys-org.title: Smart sensor identifies present molecules by remembering the past
phys-org.description: Most sensors are designed to do only one thing: detect what passes through them. But what if a sensor could do more? To create a new generation of technology, researchers have looked to living systems for inspiration. If a sensor could detect molecules, could it also remember previous interactions and selectively respond to them?

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

proj-syn.title: Africa’s Energy Curse Is a Political Choice
proj-syn.description: It is no secret why African countries with large fossil-fuel reserves nonetheless have failed to reduce extreme poverty or provide reliable electricity to all households. Those in power have made a conscious choice to privilege hard-currency export revenues, some of which then finance elite consumption rather than public investment.

proj-syn.title: The EU’s Incredible Shrinking Banking Sector
proj-syn.description: At the start of the millennium, all five of the largest European banks had a higher market capitalization than the largest US bank. What explains the fact that a quarter-century later, the largest US bank has a higher capitalization than all five top EU banks combined, and how can European policymakers address this dramatic reversal?

proj-syn.title: AI Must Enlarge the Economy, Not Divide It
proj-syn.description: To unlock AI’s full economic potential, we must steer it toward expansion. That requires replacing incentives that favor capital over labor with those that reward augmentation and investment in human capability.

proj-syn.title: Silicon, Not Software, Will Decide the AI Race
proj-syn.description: The AI race is no longer just about building better models. As competition shifts from scientific discovery to deployment, success increasingly depends on computing power, advanced semiconductors, physical infrastructure, and markets large enough to justify the enormous investments they require.

proj-syn.title: The Limits of Asia’s Two Major Growth Models
proj-syn.description: Data from a period in which both China and India pursued deliberate industrial policies show that neither country's development route is accessible to other countries. At best, their experience can alert policymakers to structural limitations and coordination problems that will require their own homegrown solutions.

proj-syn.title: The World Needs Compassionate AI
proj-syn.description: With AI having become the frontline of an intense global competition for economic and geopolitical power, speed is rewarded, scale is celebrated, and market dominance is prized above all else. Under such conditions, we risk forgetting the most important question: Whom is this intelligence ultimately meant to serve?

proj-syn.title: Trump’s New Tariffs Are an Opportunity to Fight Back
proj-syn.description: Once again, President Donald Trump is subverting domestic and international law in an effort to seize a larger fraction of global value and supply chains, and harming the US economy in the process. The longer that businesses and other governments avoid standing up to him, the greater the disaster that awaits us all.

proj-syn.title: Explaining China’s Industrial Competitiveness
proj-syn.description: External headwinds have not weakened China’s manufacturing competitiveness. That is because the Chinese economy combines an unusually large manufacturing base, deep supply chains, fast engineering feedback loops, and cutthroat domestic competition to create global powerhouses.

proj-syn.title: When Politicians Ignore Economic Expertise
proj-syn.description: As politicians encroach on areas that require technical knowledge, the risk of costly policy mistakes increases. The failures of Narendra Modi and Donald Trump show that when it comes to economic policymaking, political acumen is no substitute for a deep understanding of incentives, markets, and institutions.

proj-syn.title: The Beijing Model Meets the Brussels Effect
proj-syn.description: As Europe races to rebuild its industrial base, China is focusing more on influencing international standards and governance frameworks. The two powers are converging because neither can hope to claim a dominant position in the global energy transition by relying wholly on its traditional strengths.

proj-syn.title: The Mexican Government’s Economic Spin
proj-syn.description: By cherry-picking 12 data points that supposedly contradict top ratings agencies’ assessment of Mexico’s economy and fiscal outlook, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum recently presented a just-so story that should convince no one. A glimpse of what her list excludes makes that clear.

proj-syn.title: The Middle-Income Health Trap
proj-syn.description: Many countries that graduate from low- to middle-income status soon find themselves stuck in the position of being too rich to qualify for aid, too poor to secure reliable market-based financing, and too indebted to expand public-health spending. But it doesn't have to be this way.

proj-syn.title: Europe Is Fiddling While Rome Burns
proj-syn.description: Focusing only on emergency planning, disaster response, and recovery after each climate catastrophe is no longer enough in Europe. Policymakers urgently need to start mapping Europe’s long-term future, which will require a fundamental overhaul of its infrastructure, energy system, and major economic sectors.

proj-syn.title: Saving Democracy Requires Taxing Extreme Wealth
proj-syn.description: If lawmakers are serious about addressing the threat that dynastic wealth poses to American democracy, they can draw on considerable research that has gone into designing a wealth tax that avoids the pitfalls of other countries’ attempts. With the appearance of the world’s first trillionaire, there is no time to waste.

proj-syn.title: The AI Threat to Financial Stability
proj-syn.description: In episodes like the railroad boom and the dot-com bubble, creditors and shareholders were wiped out, because investment in a genuinely transformative technology outpaced any plausible near-term return. With the US financial system and asset markets having become a one-way bet on AI, such an outcome today could be catastrophic.

proj-syn.title: South Korea Bets on Industrial Policy Again
proj-syn.description: With industrial policy back in fashion worldwide, the question is not whether governments should intervene (they already do), but how they should proceed when they do not know in advance what will work. The answer lies in directed improvisation: creating the conditions for experimentation where it counts.
